title: Ops triage and forecast — weekly readout (May 14 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Weekly operational readout and tactical triage for GPU fleet and regional capacity. This doc captures the May 14 sync, short forecast (7d), open risks, and immediate action items for the oncall and capacity-planning squad. Informal notes: still rough, pull numbers from Fleet Dashboard before any exec share.

Attendees:
- Leila Chen (infra lead)
- Ravi Kumar (capacity planning)
- Maya Gomez (SRE oncall)
- Jon Park (release infra)
- Aisha Patel (platform ops)
- Observers: two PMs from Dedicated team (joined for roadmap context)

Agenda:
1) Quick metrics snapshot (last 7 days)
2) Region-by-region pressure points and forecast (7d)
3) Prewarming / prepositioning experiment notes
4) Autoscaling anomalies and fallback testing
5) Action items and owners

1) Metrics snapshot (summary)
- Total GPU consumption (v100-equivalent hours, 7d rolling): 85,400h (avg 12,200h/day).
- 7d growth trend: +9% week-over-week driven by two new high-throughput tenants and larger batch jobs.
- Average queue wait for spot-compatible jobs: 14m (baseline target <= 5m).
- P90 request latency on hosted API (token-level): within SLO but we saw 2 short spikes tied to regional preemption events (see incidents).

2) Regional pressure and short forecast (next 7d projection)
Note: conservative forecast assumes +10% baseline growth and a planned Dedicated beta ramp in EU.
- North America (us-west/us-east): current headrooms ~ +9% (capacity ~ 7,200h/day). Forecasted demand next week ~ 7,600-8,200h/day (risk medium).
- Europe (eu-central): capacity ~ 3,100h/day. Two Dedicated customers scheduled rollouts will add ~300-600h/day; forecasted demand 3,400-3,700h/day (risk high for eu-central if preemption or maintenance occurs).
- APAC (ap-southeast): capacity ~ 1,900h/day. Demand steady; forecast 1,950-2,100h/day (risk low).
- West-Asia edge region (new region prewarm): currently soft capacity ~ 250-450h/day (experimental nodes). Forecasted demand 600-900h/day if partner pilot spins up — we only have partial prewarm coverage (risk: high).

Quick numbers (7d forecast table, rough):
- Baseline total capacity (v100-eq/day): 12,450h
- Projected demand (conservative): 13,720h (+10%)
- Gap to cover via prewarm/burst/redistribution: ~1,270h/day

3) Prewarming & prepositioning updates
- Prewarm experiment #7 running in west-asia: results look promising for 2–5s startup latency for common small-chat workloads; cold-start long tail still logged at ~12s for larger models.
- Action: extend prewarm window for west-asia during partner pilot hours (09:00–20:00 local). Owner: Ravi. ETA: 2026-05-18.
- Note: prewarm nodes increase cost by ~6% for that region; we will measure cost per effective token to validate ROI.

4) Autoscaling anomalies and fallback testing
- Incident recap (May 12): EU autoscaler failed to respect reserved capacity when spot preemption spiked; several user jobs were pushed into fallback pool causing higher latencies. Root cause traced to a race condition in the scale-down inhibitor logic.
- Mitigation: temporary config change to lengthen scale-down grace by +60s for EU. Permanent fix targeted in PR #834 (release infra).
- Test plan: schedule canary of corrected autoscaler in eu-central (1 control plane cluster) on 2026-05-16 during low-traffic window. Owner: Jon.

5) Open risks and decision points
- Risk A: Large Dedicated rollout in EU next week. If both beta tenants ramp simultaneously, EU could be short ~600–900h/day. Contingency: prewarm + burst to other nearby regions (latency hit ~+80ms). Decision: ask Dedicated PMs to stagger by 48–72h. Owner: PMs.
- Risk B: West-Asia partner may exceed pilot expectations. We currently have soft quota; we need approval for 2 additional DGX-equivalent nodes. Request to finance for short-term burst spend. Owner: Leila -> Finance contact.
- Risk C: Preemption policy changes by cloud provider in EU (rumored) — this would increase spot eviction rate by ~2–4x. Monitoring: Maya to add eviction-rate alert with 10m cadence.

6) Action items (concrete)
- Ravi: implement extended prewarm window in west-asia + update cost dashboard. Due 2026-05-18.
- Jon: complete autoscaler race condition fix and deploy canary 2026-05-16. PR #834.
- Maya: add eviction-rate alerting and automated fallthrough test to SRE runbook. Due 2026-05-17.
- Leila: escalate short-term EU burst budget to Finance; get approval for two extra nodes if needed. Due 2026-05-16.
- Aisha: draft customer communication template for potential latency blips if rollouts are not staggered. Due 2026-05-15 (draft).

Notes to self / follow-ups (informal):
- Check whether Dedicated launch can do deployed-model throttles rather than full capacity ramps — would reduce spike.
- Revisit prewarm cost model: add per-tenant marginal cost lines for visibility in Console.
- Consider a small automation: if eu preemption-rate > 2% and dedicated ramp detected, automatically open burst nodes in us-west (controlled fallback).

Appendix: short runbook snippets (for oncall)
- If queue wait > 30m and eviction-rate > 1%:
  1) Immediately enable eu burst policy (runbook command: infra-burst enable eu-central --short-burst).
  2) Route non-latency-sensitive jobs to us-west via policy tag: "burstable".
  3) Notify PMs and CS about expected latency increase and mitigation step.

- Emergency contact list: SRE oncall (pager), Capacity (Ravi), Infra lead (Leila).

Linked tickets / references:
- JIRA-1221: EU autoscaler incident (root-cause investigation)
- PR #834: autoscaler race condition fix (release infra)
- Confluence: Fleet Forecast Dashboard (live metrics)
- Repo: ops/prewarm-experiments (experiment configs and raw logs)

End of notes.

Unresolved questions to raise in next weekly:
- Can we negotiate temporary reserved nodes with cloud provider for EU pilot? (expect finance + legal discussion)
- Should we require Dedicated beta rollouts to include a per-tenant ramp plan enforced by platform?

Status: in_review — please add comments inline on the Confluence thread or drop notes in #infra-weekly.
